analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) FOMC Review & PCE Preview, 2) ECB & BOJ Previews, 3) FX Trader Call Takeaways and 4) 5 Key Charts (29 Oct 2026)
key_insights: The FOMC held the fed funds target range at 3.75-4.00% in October. Governor Cook and President Hammack dissented, preferring a 25bp hike.
The FOMC statement upgraded its description of economic activity to expanding at a 'strong' pace (previously 'solid') and kept the language that inflation 'remains elevated'.
GS continues to expect a second and final Fed hike in December. A third hike in March is possible if inflation comes in higher than GS expects.

GS read Chairman Warsh's comments as balanced and consistent with both a slower every-other-meeting pace and a limited total number of hikes. Warsh said neither he nor most FOMC participants thought the economy was running too hot, that inflation expectations had moved in the right direction, and that financial conditions have tightened but are not tight.
GS estimates September core PCE rose 0.34% m/m (+3.11% y/y) and headline PCE rose 0.51% m/m (+3.64% y/y).

The ECB is widely expected to hold. GS expects no change to the policy language or the inflation risk assessment, and Lagarde is likely to strike a balanced message on energy-price upside risks, benign underlying inflation and tighter financial conditions.

GS maintains its forecast of one more ECB hike in December. A March hike is possible if energy prices keep rising, especially gas in a cold winter. GS sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes or a deposit rate above 3%.

GS expects the BOJ to hold the policy rate at 1.25%, seeing no need for consecutive hikes. It expects the board's core CPI forecast to be cut for FY2026 and raised for FY2027 on higher crude oil, with the upside-risk language on underlying inflation unchanged from July.

On Brazil, Alberto Ramos said the market was not positioned for the come-from-behind election win and that polls were misleading. He expects no major fiscal reform package before year-end and a primary surplus target of 0.5% of GDP, the existing 2027 target. The appointments, especially the Finance Minister, matter less than the market thinks because Lula signs off on every package.

Praneet Shah said USDJPY was the go-to hedge last week for clients with AI credit or equity exposure, with demand for 3m-6m downside binaries. JPY has a high beta within FX to an AI slowdown, and Japan's $1.3trn of US equities is a second-order support for the trade.
Shah said currencies with more rate-hike premium still to come should underperform those with little priced. EURAUD fits this and has crossed the multi-year technical break at 1.60.

Chart pack: core inflation is above target at most G10 central banks, the OBR forecasts reduce UK fiscal space, cross-asset sentiment is increasingly driven by tech, recent labour data show signs of AI-related hiring headwinds, and GS estimates AI-related capex contributed 5.0pp to Q3 measured business fixed investment growth.

risk_factors: Core inflation above target at most G10 central banks.
Energy prices rising further, especially gas in a cold winter, which could push the ECB to a March hike.
Inflation coming in higher than GS expects, which could add a third Fed hike in March.
An AI slowdown affecting credit, equities and JPY-linked positioning.
Brazil's fiscal outlook, with campaign promises in conflict with market-friendly consolidation and no appointment dates set.
UK fiscal space reduced by the OBR forecasts.

Higher energy prices and re-surging crude oil feeding inflation forecasts at the ECB and BOJ, with gas prices a risk in a cold European winter.
